title: Insulin action times

findings.where: insulin.jsx: workedText; inline diagram, accessible description and step 'worked' when params.type is 'rapid' (not pictured)
findings.title: Rapid-acting examples are falsely identified as lispro
findings.problem: workedText uses ins.eg.split(',')[0], so every rapid-acting case is labeled LISPRO. The parameters establish only the class; an aspart or glulisine question would acquire an unsupported drug identity. The default NPH screenshots conceal this error.
findings.fix: Display 'Rapid-acting insulin' unless an independently validated product name is supplied. Add tests ensuring aspart and glulisine cases cannot be relabeled lispro.

findings.where: Images 4 and 12; step 'short' caption/narration; INSULINS.short.eg and dynamicCaption
findings.title: U-100 restriction disappears from regular-insulin wording
findings.problem: The facts and table correctly restrict these times to regular U-100, but the caption and narration say 'Regular insulin given subcutaneously' and then 'Given IV.' The short step hides the note containing the U-500 exception. This makes the spoken claim broader than the intended product: regular U-500 has different action times and must not be administered IV. Generated short-acting worked captions also omit U-100.
findings.fix: Specify 'regular U-100' in the caption, narration and generated worked labels. Explicitly attach the IV comparison to regular U-100 rather than regular insulin generally.

assessment: Revise before publishing. The worked-example logic invents a specific rapid-acting drug, and the regular-insulin narration drops a safety-critical concentration qualifier.
